chapter: Coleman Hawkins, Bernie Young and doubling on tenor
title: Picking the clarinet up again; Prince Robinson
summary: He estimates four months to get back on clarinet; Dance recalls Prince Robinson sounding rusty on a recording, and Caldwell recalls him doubling with Snowden.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, I was thinking the same thing. You know, it's a funny thing that -- well, how much would it take you to sort of pick up the clarinet and work on it?
Oh, I think about four months.

Yeah, because I noticed, you know, For Camden I made a record with Andy Gibson (unintelligible), oh, it must be nearly ten years now, you know, and he did the arrangement, and I said I want so and so. And so he said, well then, you have so and so. Then I've got to have so and so. So this --
-- he had a guy on it (unintelligible) baritone that I'd never heard of. (unintelligible) you know, he played with Katum's band. Leslie Johnkings M. White
But on clarinet he had Prince Robinson Robertson.
Well, Prince, he sounded fine, but he was rusty, you know. He hadn't played the clarinet, you know, so there were squeaks, but what he played was very nice.
Oh, he was -- yes, he was.
You know, he wasn't up on the --
Yeah, because we played clarinet -- doubled on clarinet and tenor when -- when he was with Snowden Snowden Elmer Storden's band. So Elmer Storden had a job -- two jobs -- one at the Nest Nest Club --
